picks.style: ancient greek threnody, lyre and low reed, grave male voice, slow, pleading, shadowed
picks.why: Almost pure quoted verse — the unburied dead begging for a grave and a tear, and the boy pleading to keep the light.

picks.style: gnomic chant, kithara and hand drum, stern measured voice, moderate, admonitory, turning
picks.why: The Atreus lines inverted into their better form — joy and grief by turns, and no one an unchanged favourite of Fate.

picks.style: roman rustic elegy, lyre and soft double pipe, warm intimate male voice, unhurried, pastoral, contented
picks.why: 'Let another heap up riches' against a life of quiet poverty and a steady hearth-fire — the whole Tibullan creed, and his most famous opening.

picks.style: latin elegy of consolation, plucked lyre and low drone, weary tender voice, slow, building through repetition
picks.why: Hope feeds the farmers, catches the birds, consoles the fettered man who sings at his work — anaphora made for a refrain.

picks.style: roman peace-hymn, aulos and frame drum, pleading male voice with soft chorus, moderate, aching, resolving
picks.why: 'Four times blessed is he at whom a tender girl can weep' turning into the invocation of Peace with her corn-ear.

picks.style: augustan comic recitative, harpsichord and pizzicato strings, sly conversational tenor, brisk, mock-serious
picks.why: Cupid reading the title and crying 'Treason!' — a complete comic scene that sets up the whole poem.

picks.style: tragic ballad, solo cello and guitar, low grieving female voice, slow, unsteady, hushed
picks.why: Phyllis on the ninth day at the shore — 'She offers, and flies back, dreads what she dares' — devastating and self-contained.

picks.style: resolute farewell air, lute and viol, firm baritone, measured, ceremonial, cold
picks.why: Burning the old love-letters: 'Be this the fun'ral pile of my desire; Perish, my love, in this just flame expire.'

picks.style: georgian satirical patter song, harpsichord and pizzicato strings, arch narrating soprano, brisk, gossipy, biting
picks.why: The drawing-room demolishing a servant's book — 'there's something about a mad cow' — the poem she is remembered for.

picks.style: drawing-room comedy song, spinet and clattering percussion, quick wry female voice, chattering, clipped, ironic
picks.why: The tea-party opening of the same satire — cowslip wine that would pass for Champaign, and crests instead of poetry.

picks.style: rustic courtship ballad, fiddle and hammered dulcimer, plain country voice, jog-trot, dry, strophic
picks.why: The clumsy love letter and two apples: 'Which Nell receiv'd, and read the letter, (But she lik'd the apples better)'.

picks.style: georgian theatre song, harpsichord and flute, sincere clear tenor, gentle, strophic, courting
picks.why: A real song to Sylvia, turning on blossoms falling so the ripening fruit appears — beauty decaying while the mind improves.

picks.style: comic macabre ballad, bassoon and plucked strings, dry conspiratorial baritone, moderate, sardonic, sidling
picks.why: Death drops in on a struggling doctor for a friendly chat — 'we both are losers if you fail'.

picks.style: mock-epitaph air, spinet and recorder, light mischievous soprano, quick, teasing, birdlike
picks.why: The dead bullfinch promising to haunt the household as a tell-tale bird and sing every tale to Lucy.

picks.style: english satirical ballad, fiddle and hurdy-gurdy, sardonic male voice, rolling anapestic swing, strophic with refrain
picks.why: Every profession excused by the same closing line — 'he but lives by his trade' — a refrain that is already written.

picks.style: broadside ballad finale, fiddle and drum, wry male voice, rolling, resigned, closing hard
picks.why: The satire turns on its author — 'Cheat myself by my rhyming, and starve by my trade'.

picks.style: georgian parlour song, lute and viola, tender light tenor, gentle, courting, small-scale
picks.why: Chloe's pricked finger made into Cupid's arrow, then the sharper joke of venal Belinda and Charon's fee.

picks.style: sanskrit philosophical chant, tanpura drone and small cymbals, deep steady male voice, slow, austere, sparse
picks.why: The one candidate with a real image — the whole vast doctrine held brief and undiminished, as in a mirror.
